texts.full_text: epithelium: a time-resolved fluorescence spectroscopy study. The photophysical properties of purified populations of melanin and lipofuscin granules from human retinal pigment epithelium, and their changes with donor age, have been investigated using high-sensitivity time-resolved fluorescence spectroscopy techniques with picosecond gating capabilities. The overall fluorescence intensity of both melanin and lipofuscin granules clearly increased with increasing donor age. The findings suggest that the photophysical properties of purified populations of melanin and lipofuscin granules from human retinal pigment tissue underwent dramatic transformations as a function of donor age. Additionally, the fluorescence sensitivity of both melanin and lipofuscin granules was reported to improve with decreasing donor age, indicating an accumulation or aggregation of these pigments over time. However, study of the photophysical properties showed that the emission spectrum moved towards longer frequencies (blue-shifted) as a function of donor age. This change in spectral position is consistent with shifts in the cellular composition and organization of melanin and lipofuscin granules due to aging-related oxidative stress and cellular damage. The findings therefore suggest that lipofuscin granules exhibit more pronounced photobleaching behaviour compared to purified populations of melanin, which could be linked to variations in their molecular structure or mechanical properties. Not giving up is something Tracy Kemper-Hermann, of GRASP (Grief Recovery After A Substance Passing), spoke of as well. Kemper-Hermann lost her husband, Jason, to an accidental overdose in 2014. "Somehow even in death we're still fighting this fight," said Kemper Hermann. "I'm here to let everybody know, let our community know this is a disease. This is preventable."
